subject: Acme - hybrid on-prem egress blackhole / NAT routing review
messages:
From: Raj Kapoor <raj.kapoor@acme.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, ops@acme.com
Cc: Tina Alvarez <tina.alvarez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent egress blackhole after firewall rule sync to on-prem appliance

Hi Soojin / Redwood team,

We rolled the updated firewall rule-set last night as part of the hybrid migration cutover. Since the change, ~15% of requests from our app tier to Redwood Private endpoints are timing out. From our side: traceroutes to the Redwoods ingress show traffic reaches the upstream transit but stops before the FW cluster (see attached). The issue looks intermittent (spikes for ~30s every few minutes).

What we've done so far:
- Confirmed route tables in our VPC point to the transit gateway for the 10.20.0.0/16 prefix that Redwood provided.
- Confirmed SNAT rules exist on the firewall, but the counters are low and not increasing during timeouts.
- MTU on our end is set to 1500; we haven't changed it during the cutover.

This is causing production errors for a small percentage of requests (we're seeing retries and timeouts in our monitoring). Can you confirm whether Redwood saw any capacity or routing changes on their side around 02:00 UTC? We're escalating since this coincides with the migration window.

I've attached: acme_traceroute_to_redwood_gateway.txt, firewall_policy_export_20260418.json, and a snapshot of the NAT table.

Thanks,
Raj Kapoor
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Kapoor <raj.kapoor@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress blackhole after firewall rule sync to on-prem appliance

Thanks Raj — and sorry you're seeing this. We're pulling Network Eng and Infra on the thread.

Quick acknowledgement and immediate asks so we can triage:
- Can you share a short tcpdump (first 100 packets) on the firewall WAN interface when you observe a timeout window? That will help us see SYN/SYN-ACK patterns and any RSTs.
- Confirm whether the Transit Gateway in your account is doing asymmetric routing for return traffic (we've seen TGW policy changes cause occasional blackhole behavior).
- If possible, toggle a single test host to use an alternate SNAT IP (we suspect SNAT exhaustion/asymmetric SNAT mapping).

From Redwood side: Michael, can you start by checking whether our edge seen any route flaps or NAT gateway CPU/conntrack pressure around 02:00 UTC? Also check if our egress ACLs changed for Acme's prefix.

I'll be available for a quick bridge — propose 30 mins at 10:45 PT if that works for Acme.

Regards,
So ojin Lee
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0129

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Raj Kapoor <raj.kapoor@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress blackhole after firewall rule sync to on-prem appliance

Thanks for the details, Raj. Initial checks from our edge and infra:
- No config pushes on Redwood edge for Acme's prefix at ~02:00 UTC.
- Per-edge telemetry: minor packet drops observed on a small subset of connections (~0.3% of flows) with retransmit spikes coincident with the windows you described — consistent with either MTU issues or intermittent asymmetric routing.
- Our conntrack/NAT pools are not exhausted on the Redwood side. CPU and conntrack usage are nominal.

Preliminary troubleshooting checklist (things that commonly cause this after a firewall sync):
1) MTU / PMTUD: if the firewall is fragmenting/blackholing ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages, large responses can silently fail. Please confirm whether you have ICMP rate-limiting or filtering on the WAN interface.
2) Asymmetric return path: ensure your TGW and VPC route tables return traffic to the same firewall path the request took.
3) SNAT port exhaustion: even if counters look ok, short bursts from many ephemeral sockets can temporarily exhaust ports on a SNAT IP. Test by assigning a second SNAT IP to a test host.
4) Firewall health / session table: some appliance firmware versions have heuristics that drop sporadic flows under load — the export you attached will help.
5) Security group / NACL mismatch: confirm there isn't a deny rule on the return path for ephemeral ports (1024-65535).

If you can provide tcpdump (WAN interface) and a short pcap from a failing host, we can correlate with our edge traces. If PMTUD is likely, a quick test: lower MTU to 1400 on a test host and retest.

I'll stand up packet capture correlation between 02:00-02:30 UTC and feed results into this thread.

-Michael
Michael Grant
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai

From: Raj Kapoor <raj.kapoor@acme.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tina Alvarez <tina.alvarez@acme.com>, ops@acme.com
Date: 2026-04-18T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress blackhole after firewall rule sync to on-prem appliance

Thanks Michael — attaching the captures and exports you asked for. Notes from our side:
- tcpdump on the firewall WAN during a spike shows SYNs leaving to Redwood, but we only see SYNs (no SYN-ACKs) returned to the firewall for a subset of flows. Packet counts align with the traceroute: path reaches the upstream transit and disappears.
- Firewall export indicates no notable CPU/health flags; session table shows many short-lived sessions but not clearly exhausted.
- We do filter ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) for rate-limiting, but not outright drop.

Attachments: acme_traceroute_to_redwood_gateway.txt, firewall_policy_export_20260418.json, nat_table_snapshot.txt, acme_wan_tcpdump.pcap (referenced; we've uploaded to the ticket).

Happy to join the 10:45 PT bridge.

- Raj

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Kapoor <raj.kapoor@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress blackhole after firewall rule sync to on-prem appliance

Thanks Raj — got the attachments and tcpdump link. Next steps for our bridge at 10:45 PT:
- Michael will correlate the pcaps with our edge packet captures and surface whether we see RSTs or PMTUD ICMP being blocked.
- Lauren will validate our outbound ACLs and confirm no transient route flap on Redwood egress.
- Acme to test lowering MTU to 1400 on one test host and to assign an alternate SNAT IP for a small subset of sessions (we'll verify port mapping behavior).

If we confirm PMTUD/ICMP suppression as the root cause, remediation options: allow ICMP 'fragmentation needed' across the WAN interface, or use lowered MTU on the firewall/transit attachment as a temporary mitigation. If instead we confirm asymmetric routing, we will coordinate immediate route table changes and a rollback of the firewall change if required.

I'll start the bridge and share a short runbook of commands we may ask you to run. Appreciate the fast turnaround here — we'll aim for a mitigation within 60 minutes of the bridge.

Regards,
So ojin Lee
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
